Question: What orders did the High Court give in Kinyua Maingi Advocates v Trident Insurance Company Limited regarding the applicant's out-of-time reference?

The High Court granted the applicant leave to file its reference out of time, ordered that the reference be served within seven days, stayed execution of the decree pending determination of the reference, and required the decretal sum to be deposited in a joint account within thirty days. Remuneration Order. Section 51(2) of the Advocates Act provides that;
“The certicate of the taxing ocer by whom any bill has been taxed shall, unless it is set

court may make such order in relation thereto as it thinks t, including, in a case where the
retainer is not disputed, an order that judgment be entered for the sum certied to be due
with costs”.
11. On jurisdiction, Section 2 of the Advocates Act denes court to mean “High Court”. That means that
it is only the “High Court” that has the jurisdiction to set aside or alter a certicate of costs and/or
ascertain the amount taxed to be correct and convert the same into judgement.

Public Service Commission possess the exclusive constitutional mandate to receive, consider, and
approve Human Resource Instruments of State Corporations
The consolidated petitions challenged an advisory letter issued by the Attorney General on 27th July 2023 and
a subsequent circular by the State Corporations Advisory Committee dated 8th August 2023. The petitioners
contended that the impugned communications unlawfully interfered with the constitutional mandate of the
Public Service Commission under Article 234 of the Constitution. They argued that employees of state corporations
and public universities formed part of the public service and therefore fell within the Commission’s jurisdiction
on matters of human resource management, terms of service, and organisational structures. The High Court held
that the Attorney General’s advice carried constitutional significance and could not be casually disregarded by
State or public officers without cogent, rational, and publicly justifiable reasons. It emphasized that the Attorney
General functioned as the legal conscience of the State and that capricious rejection of such advice undermined
https://new.kenyalaw.org/akn/ke/judgment/kehc/2025/18054/eng@2025-12-05 1

impugned advisory and circular were unconstitutional or that they unlawfully usurped the mandate of the Public
Service Commission. Consequently, the Court declined to grant the declaratory and prerogative orders sought.

Constitutional Law – Office of the Attorney General – function – principal legal advisor to the Government

Question: In the case Kenya Union of Domestic Hotels Education and Allied, what did the court hold about the application of Article 232(2) to state corporations, and which constitutional principle did it invoke?

The court held that Article 232(2)(b) applies to all state corporations, so the values and principles of public service must govern their employees just as they do state organs [chunk_id: Kenya Union of Domestic Hotels Education and Allied  (Kudhehia Workers) v Salaries and Renumeration Commission  another (Constitutional Application 294of2013) 2014KEHC8148(KLR) (Constitutional and Human Rights) (25July2014) (Judgment)__s4__c10, Kenya Union of Domestic Hotels Education and Allied]. It invoked the rule of harmony, citing Tinyefuza v Attorney General Constitutional Appeal NO. 1 of 1997, and noted that state corporations are public entities established by the President under the State Corporations Act with a controlling stake by the state [chunk_id: Kenya Union of Domestic Hotels Education and Allied  (Kudhehia Workers) v Salaries and Renumeration Commission  another (Constitutional Application 294of2013) 2014KEHC8148(KLR) (Constitutional and Human Rights) (25July2014) (Judgment)__s4__c10, Kenya Union of Domestic Hotels Education and Allied].

April 2020.
[8] For all the foregoing, it is clear that the appellant’s conduct was all along bent at having the matter concluded at the highest level
possible and believed that it had strong legal grounds to challenge the original judgment of the lower court and all subsequent orders and
decisions arising therefrom at both the lower and High courts. In the circumstances, it cannot be said that the appellant was not and has
never been diligent in having this matter concluded in one way or the other. Given its past conduct, the delay of two years in not prosecuting
the appeal cannot be construed to mean that the appellant was indolent or that he acted in bad faith to deliberately delay the expeditious
disposal of this matter and/or to prevent the respondent (PLAINTIFF) from enjoying the fruits of this judgment. It is for all these reason,
that the court deems it necessary and just to exercise its discretion in favour of the appellant/applicant and allow the present application on
condition that the intended appeal be filed in the Court of Appeal at Kisumu within the next fourteen (14) days from this date hereof. In
default, the leave granted shall forthwith lapse and the respondent be at liberty to execute the necessary decree.
